1.explanation: This minimal example shows how to reproduce the bug: we attach a normal right-click handler to the container. On every right-click we compute a fake DOMRect object (using the click’s clientX/Y) and hand it to Carbon’s Popover as the targetRef. Because the Popover expects a real element or an object with getBoundingClientRect, failing to supply one (or supplying an invalid one) causes the bubble never to appear in the correct location. Running this code in a fresh Create React App (or CodeSandbox) will surface the same issue you saw: the Popover either never opens, or it opens in the top-left corner instead of at the mouse location. You can now step through the Popover logic in Carbon to see why the positioning call fails and how to patch it.
1.bug_scenario: In our sandbox we are trying to build a true right-click (context) menu using Carbon’s floating menu primitives (Popover/OverflowMenu), but nothing ever appears at the mouse position. In the first image you can see a tree of nested items (Files → Cloud computing → Containers) and we expect a menu to pop up on right-click, yet the popup never renders at the click coordinates. In subsequent GIFs you can see attempts to use Popover, Dropdown, and OverflowMenu—in each case the menu either never opens or is always pinned to (0,0) because there is no valid targetRef.
